items.why: The viewer got the fear of being seen as flawed, which matches the narration, though the mask-slipping idea is only implied.
Thawing and opening up matches the narration's thaw and her longing to be seen, though the desire part is missed.
Hiding something from her mother matches the narration directly, though the lover and happiness are not conveyed.
Sitting alone on a sad birthday misses that Hannah is quietly indifferent to her mother's staged world, so the mood reads different from the narration.
A father hiding his terror matches the narration exactly.
Awkward compliance is captured, but the hidden horror and brokenness beneath the mask is missing.
A girl with no friends her age matches the narration's lack of socialization.
The narration says Blue hides nothing and Jake validates her, but the viewer reads Laurel as a woman on the phone getting confirmation, so the person and the point of Blue's openness are lost.
A man who orchestrated the discovery matches Floyd being behind the finding of Ellie's remains.
